source_title: The new rules of management | India's Best B-Schools - India Today
source_excerpt:
In the age of artificial intelligence, a traditional MBA degree cannot be just a passport to a well-paying consultancy job but must instead teach students the value of human judgement, imagination and adaptability
F or decades, the MBA promised a simple bargain. Master management, secure a campus placement and enter the corporate fast track. That bargain has not collapsed, but it is being rewritten. Artificial intelligence can perform tasks once entrusted by freshly minted managers. Employers want skills beyond a de gree. Students want to know whether the returns justify the costs.
Warning signs are emerging. Registrations for the Common Admission Test (CAT) fell from 329,000 in 2024 to 295,000 in 2025. In India Today’s Best B-School survey of 2026, 40 per cent of the top 25 B-schools reported lower admissions. These included four IIMs. Abroad, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Arizona State University and Britain’s Henley Busi ness School have dropped the full-time two-year MBA. Aswath Damodaran of NYU Stern predicts fewer bankers, consultants and investment managers as AI advances, and consequently few er takers for management degrees. His prescription is radical. Stop expanding and cut the MBA to one year.
India is not there yet. A degree from a leading B-school costs Rs 20-40 lakh, but corporate demand remains strong. Still, the question of value has become unavoidable. The 14th india today-MDRA survey contacted over 2,000 institutions and ranked 277 on 127 attributes spanning learning, placements, future orientation, campus life and governance. It also exam ined executive, online, advanced-management and doctoral programmes.
At the top, IIM Ahmedabad retains first place, followed by IIM Calcutta and Lucknow, SPJIMR Mumbai and XLRI Jamshedpur. But familiar rankings conceal divergent fortunes. The top 25’s placement rate slipped from 97.5 to 96.4 per cent, while that of schools ranked 51-75 rose from 87.4 to 93.8 per cent. Average domestic salaries at the top 10 have almost doubled since 2015 to Rs 29.9 lakh per year. For schools ranked 76-100, they fell this year to Rs 7.26 lakh.
Stability at the top also hides churn inside classrooms. Engineers comprised 84 per cent of students at the top 25 schools in 2015. Today, they account for 40 per cent. Women’s representation has risen from 27.8 to 37.5 per cent. Damo daran says he finds it easier to teach 100 history majors to value companies than to persuade 100 engineers to trust their imagination. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, the lone history graduate in his XLRI class, learnt to frame problems, weigh the cost of inaction and commit.
Other distinguished alumni enjoy these lessons. World Bank president ajay Banga says IIM Ahmedabad taught him to "define the real problem before trying to solve it". Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran recalls learning to decide without perfect information".
Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi credits IIM Calcutta with teaching her to hold my own in a room full of men and translate classroom concepts into real-world solutions.
Al makes these human capabilities more valuable. "For us, the biggest change is a shift from teaching analysis to teaching judgement, says IIM Ahmedabad Director Bharat Bhasker. His institute has launched the Rs 100 crore-endowed Krishnamurthy Tandon School of AI. IIM Calcutta has earmarked over Rs 50 crore for IT upgrades and AI labs, with a two-year online MBA planned for 2027.
The survey finds a 60 per cent rise in successful start-ups associated with the top 25 B-schools, suggesting another measure of success beyond placement packages. The MBA’s future lies not in teaching what machines can already do, but in developing the imagination, adaptability and moral courage to decide what should be done.
T he 2026 India Today Group survey of the country’s business schools was conducted by Delhi-based market research firm Marketing & Development Research Associates (MDRA). The ranking provides the most credible and exhaustive rankings of India’s Best B-schools based on the most recent data. The ranking provides a comprehensive analysis of key areas, clearly highlighting which courses are best suited for different categories of aspirants. As management education evolves, we have expanded our rankings to serve distinct audiences. This year, too, dedicated rankings are being presented for Top Executive Programmes, Top Advanced Management Programmes (for professionals with over 10 years of experience), Top Executive Fellow Programmes in Management (EFPMs), Top On-campus Fellow Programmes in Management (FPMs/PhDs) and the Top Online MBAs in India.
Full-time MBA/ PGDM ranking: A comprehensive list of B-schools, offering full-time classroom management programmes (PGDM/ MBA), established at least five years ago and with a minimum of three graduated batches, was drawn for the rankings. An objective questionnaire was finetuned to obtain the latest relevant information from the institutes on 127 attributes to give stakeholders more realistic, updated and accurate information. More than 2,000 B-schools across India, fulfilling the qualification criteria for participation, were contacted, 279 of them responded within the deadline, and 277 eligible ones fulfilling the qualifying criteria were ranked.
After receiving the objective data, four processes—data cleaning logical checks, validation, back-checks and audits—were conducted. In the first stage, each aspect of the details provided by the B-schools was carefully examined through available information and database available with MDRA. In the second stage, verification and audits of the participating B-schools were conducted by MDRA researchers to ensure accuracy and correctness of the data submitted. For decades, the MBA promised a simple bargain. Master management, secure a campus placement and enter the corporate fast track. That bargain has not collapsed, but it is being rewritten. Artificial intelligence can perform tasks once entrusted to freshly minted managers. Employers want skills beyond a degree. Students want to know whether the returns justify the costs.
The five key parameters of evaluation were Learning Experience, Living Experience, Selection Process, Placement Performance and Future Orientation (see box). The scores of these parameters were then summed up to get the total objective score of each institute. The final rank was assigned to B-schools based on objective data after various levels of cross-validation through multiple sources and physical audits.
To reflect India’s regional diversity and students’ preferences, the overall rankings were used to create separate zonal, parameter-wise and return on investment (RoI) rankings. A Top Emerging MBA Courses list recognises newer institutions whose first batch graduated after 2015. This year also introduces the Most Improved B-schools category, highlighting institutions that have made significant gains in the ITG-MDRA rankings over the past five years. The B-school with the highest percentage improvement in rank over the five-year period tops the list, followed by others in descending order of improvement.
Executive Programmes: Indian B-schools offer an enormous variety of executive programmes—ranging from entry-level options to courses designed for leaders with 15+ years of experience. They differ widely in focus (general management, industry-specific or functional specialisations), curriculum, pedagogy, delivery models (hybrid or direct-to-device), faculty quality, alumni access and fees. These programmes do not confer an MBA or equivalent degree.
For this ranking, meant for a broad audience, we considered only long-established, rigorous general management programmes from top institutes. The evaluation was based solely on objective data gathered through secondary research, using parameters such as programme fees, institute reputation, course continuity, weekly interaction load, eligibility criteria, number of online/ offline sessions and overall pedagogy. The top 15 executive programmes were then ranked on this basis.
Advanced Management Programme (AMPs): The AMP rankings are based entirely on objective data from extensive secondary research. Only programmes meant for senior professionals with at least 10 years of work experience were included to maintain relevance and comparability. These AMPs target leaders and strategic decision-makers, and are delivered in blended or fully online formats to suit executive schedules. Most run for 10-12 months, except ISB’s Global AMP, which is a five-month programme. The evaluation considered key parameters such as programme fees, duration, delivery mode, faculty strength, institutional reputation, eligibility criteria, course continuity, alumni profile and overall programme design. Together, these metrics provided a comprehensive and balanced assessment of India’s leading AMPs.
Online MBAs: The Online MBA rankings are based solely on objective data from secondary research. Only two-year online or blended programmes from recognised B-schools—leading to a valid master’s or postgraduate degree/diploma—were included. Though institutions market them as Executive MBA, Online MBA or Online PGDM, these programmes share a common goal: offering an MBA-equivalent qualification without requiring learners to leave their jobs. Unlike AMPs, they cater to a broader audience, with work-experience requirements varying across schools. The evaluation drew on parameters such as programme fees, campus immersion, degree recognition, eligibility norms, faculty quality, institutional reputation, class frequency and duration, course continuity, alumni engagement, placement outcomes and delivery mode. This framework ensured a rigorous assessment of academic quality, credibility, delivery effectiveness and career impact.
Executive Fellow Programmes in Management (EFPMs): The Executive FPM rankings were derived entirely from objective, verified secondary data. Key parameters included programme fees, PhD equivalence and recognition, entrance requirements, work-experience norms, institutional reputation, alumni strength, faculty quality, research output (scholars enrolled and graduated), and research/ consultancy projects over the past three years. This framework enabled a balanced assessment of academic rigour, research depth, faculty capability and institutional strength. These programmes—commonly called Executive FPMs but also offered as Executive Doctoral Programmes or PhDs for Working Professionals—are all PhD-equivalent. They require at least a master’s degree with relevant work experience, run for 3 to 6 years, and are delivered in blended or online formats to suit working executives.
Fellow Programmes in Management (FPMs)/ PhD in Management: The FPM/ PhD rankings were developed entirely through secondary research using credible public sources, including institute websites, admission brochures, annual reports and official notifications. Programmes were evaluated across a broad set of academic and research parameters: programme fees, eligibility norms, required entrance exams (CAT, GMAT, GRE, UGC-NET etc.), and stipend structures across Slabs I-III. Additional benefits—HRA (with/ without family), computer and contingency allowances, and domestic/ international conference support—were also assessed.
Research strength was measured through the number of scholars currently enrolled and graduated (up to 2023-24), sponsored and consultancy projects and their funding amounts, and total faculty strength. Institutional reputation was captured through the latest Business Today B-School ranking. All indicators were normalised and weighted to create a composite score, ensuring a transparent, balanced, and data-driven evaluation of India’s leading FPM/ PhD programmes in management.
A large team comprising researchers, statisticians, econometricians and analysts worked on this project from April 2026 to September 2026. The MDRA core team, led by Abhishek Agrawal (CEO), comprised Abnish Jha (Senior Project Director), Vaibhav Gupta (Research Manager), Manveer Singh (Assistant Manager EDP), Robin Singh (Research Executive) and Rishav Sharma (Research Executive).
